answers.answer: Vitest is a Vite-powered testing framework: assertions, snapshots, mocking/spies, watch mode, coverage, browser/component testing and benchmarks. Test authors import its testing API; developers run npx vitest or package scripts, and CI runs the repository's test scripts. Programmatic integrations can use vitest/node. The executable package entry is vitest.mjs, which imports dist/cli.js; its source calls createCLI().parse().

Principal packages: vitest supplies the framework, CLI and public Node/runtime/worker interfaces; @vitest/expect implements Jest-style matchers atop Chai; snapshot manages snapshots; spy implements spies; mocker handles module mocking; utils supplies shared helpers; pretty-format supplies ESM-compatible value formatting. browser runs browser tests, browser-playwright provides Playwright integration, and browser-preview uses a chosen browser. coverage-v8 and coverage-istanbul are separate coverage providers. ui supplies the visual interface/reporting entry; web-worker supplies Web Worker test support. These are package boundaries, not claims that every package is loaded by parseCLI.

The inspected implementation is TypeScript, with JavaScript/ESM launch and Rollup configuration files; JSON manifests and YAML define package/workspace structure, and Markdown holds documentation. pnpm organizes packages/*, examples/*, test/* and docs. The private root orchestrates recursive builds, TypeScript checks and tests. Rollup builds the Vitest library/CLI into dist ESM and declaration outputs, with a separate CJS config output. Browser/UI client builds use Vite; the UI additionally uses Vue tooling. package.json exports define public subpaths, while workspace:* dependencies connect packages.

The documented library entry is import { parseCLI } from 'vitest/node'. The vitest package export './node' resolves normally to dist/node.js (types: dist/node.d.ts), or to src/public/node.ts under __vitest_source__. That source barrel re-exports parseCLI from ../node/cli/cac. Rollup's node entry is src/public/node.ts. Thus the implementation begins in cac.ts, not in the executable's automatic parse path.
In cac.ts, parseCLI calls createCLI(config).parse(arrayArgs, { run: false }), then sets options.run=true when arrayArgs[2] is 'run' and options.watch is falsy. It returns filter/options.

Runtime internal dependencies: @vitest/utils/helpers; ../../utils/env; ./cli-config; ./completions; package version JSON. Dynamic runtime imports additionally reach ./cli-api, ../reporters/renderers/utils, ./doctor, and ../../create/browser/creator. Type-only imports are excluded. cac, pathe and tinyrainbow are external packages.

Path: public re-export → parseCLI → splitArgv → createCLI → external CAC parse with execution disabled → run-option postprocessing → return. The pinned test expects {filter:[], options:{run:true,'--':[],color:true}}. Registered test-running actions are not invoked. CAC's external parser and the external completion adapter remain untraced boundaries; this is source/test evidence, not an observed execution.

Direct callers evidenced are node/cli.ts's top-level createCLI().parse(), parseCLI in cac.ts, and the unit test's top-level const vitestCli=createCLI(). The public node.ts barrel re-exports it, and advanced documentation demonstrates direct library consumption. The map reported only the first two exact call edges; the test source establishes the additional caller. External consumers are not exhaustively known.

test/unit/test/cli-test.test.ts registers 'public parseCLI works correctly' (406-567). It imports parseCLI through vitest/node and directly asserts 'vitest run' produces run:true, empty filters, '--':[], color:true. Its 'vitest run --watch' case expects watch:true and w:true without run:true; dev/watch cases also check watch handling. This tests the public wrapper, unlike nearby getCLIOptions tests using a shared createCLI parser. test/unit package scripts enter through vitest, including project-specific threads/forks/vmThreads scripts. Tests were inspected, not executed.

String argv enters parseCLI's string branch. splitArgv protects whitespace inside quoted substrings with NULs, splits on literal spaces, restores spaces and removes surrounding quotes. parseCLI validates 'vitest', substitutes '/index.js', prepends 'node', parses, postprocesses command options, and returns filters/options.
